questions.skill: Construct a scatter plot for bivariate measurement data
questions.prompt: Seven students recorded (hours studied, test score): (1, 50), (2, 60), (3, 60), (4, 70), (5, 80), (6, 80), (7, 90) Make a scatter plot of the data on the grid.
questions.prompt_markup:
Seven students recorded (hours studied, test score):
(1, 50), (2, 60), (3, 60), (4, 70), (5, 80), (6, 80), (7, 90)
Make a scatter plot of the data on the grid.

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 8 and y from 0 to 100. x-axis label "Hours studied", y-axis label "Test score". Nothing is plotted; the student draws on it.

questions.skill: Construct a scatter plot for bivariate measurement data
questions.prompt: The scatter plot should show the data (1, 6), (2, 5), (3, 5), (5, 3), and (7, 2), but one point is plotted wrong. Which point is wrong, and where should it be?
questions.prompt_markup:
The scatter plot should show the data (1, 6), (2, 5), (3, 5), (5, 3), and (7, 2), but one point is plotted wrong.
Which point is wrong, and where should it be?
questions.correct_answer: The pair (7, 2) is plotted at (2, 7). It should be 7 units right and 2 units up, at (7, 2).

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 8 and y from 0 to 8. x-axis label "x", y-axis label "y". Points: (1, 6), (2, 5), (3, 5), (5, 3), (2, 7).

sections.skill: Represent two-variable data on a scatter plot and describe how the variables are related

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Represent two-variable data on a scatter plot and describe how the variables are related
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: draw on the figure and write an answer
questions.prompt: Six used bikes have these (age in years, value in tens of dollars): (1, 20), (2, 17), (3, 15), (4, 12), (5, 10), (6, 8) Make a scatter plot of the data. Then describe how age and value are related.
questions.prompt_markup:
Six used bikes have these (age in years, value in tens of dollars):
(1, 20), (2, 17), (3, 15), (4, 12), (5, 10), (6, 8)
Make a scatter plot of the data. Then describe how age and value are related.
questions.correct_answer: As age increases, value decreases: a negative linear association.

figure.description: Coordinate grid with x from 0 to 7 and y from 0 to 22. x-axis label "Age (years)", y-axis label "Value ($10s)". Nothing is plotted; the student draws on it.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data

questions.prompt: A scatter plot of hours of sleep and reaction time shows points falling from left to right. Describe how the variables are related.
questions.prompt_markup:

questions.correct_answer: As sleep increases, reaction time tends to decrease (a negative association).
